subject: environmental
audience: FE Environmental candidates and environmental engineering students
title: The Contact Tank That Had Only 21 Effective Minutes
featured_title: THE CONTACT TANK THAT HAD ONLY 21 EFFECTIVE MINUTES

presentation.challenge: The hydraulic detention time was 30 minutes, but baffling reduced the effective contact time to 21 minutes. The CT value was 31.5, not 45.

practice.primary_question: How do tank volume, flow, baffling factor, disinfectant residual, and effective contact time determine CT?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Using nominal theoretical detention time directly in a CT calculation even when an effective-contact-time or baffling correction is explicitly specified.

case_dna.target_misconception: A 30-minute theoretical detention time means the disinfectant has 30 minutes of effective contact even when a baffling factor of 0.70 is given.
case_dna.why_plausible: Tank volume divided by flow gives a valid nominal detention time, so it is easy to stop before applying the stated hydraulic correction.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: For V=0.50 MG and Q=24 MGD, nominal detention is 30 min. With baffling factor 0.70, effective contact time is 21 min; at 1.5 mg/L residual, CT=31.5 mg·min/L.
case_dna.corrected_model: When the problem specifies an effective-time factor, calculate theoretical detention time from V/Q, multiply by that factor, then compute CT=C×t_effective.

problem_statement: A disinfection contact tank has a volume of 0.50 MG and treats 24 MGD. The measured disinfectant residual is 1.5 mg/L. The stated baffling factor is 0.70, defined here as effective contact time divided by theoretical detention time. A note uses the full theoretical detention time and reports CT=45 mg·min/L. Determine the correct effective contact time and CT.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The tank volume was correct. The usable contact time was overstated.
gates.prompt: What must be applied after calculating V/Q?

options.label: Compute t_theoretical=V/Q, then t_effective=0.70t_theoretical, then CT=Ct_effective
options.reason: This follows the factor definition stated in the problem.

options.label: Use CT=C(V/Q) without the baffling factor
options.reason: That ignores the explicit effective-contact-time correction.

options.label: Divide theoretical time by 0.70
options.reason: The problem defines the factor as effective time divided by theoretical time, so effective time is smaller.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict the effective contact time
gates.prompt: Enter the effective contact time in minutes.

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Track water through the contact basin
gates.result: The effective contact time is 21 minutes.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the CT value
gates.success: The theoretical detention time is 30 min, effective time is 21 min, and CT is 31.5 mg·min/L.
gates.hint: Convert V/Q from days to minutes with 1440 min/day before applying the baffling factor.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: Hydraulic inefficiency reduces usable contact time

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the disinfection note
report: C1. The theoretical detention time is 30 min.
C3. Therefore the effective time is 30 min and CT is 45 mg·min/L.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: This is the stated hydraulic correction.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: It ignores the baffling factor when converting theoretical detention time to effective contact time.

evidence_choices.label: 0.70×30=21 min and 1.5×21=31.5 mg·min/L
evidence_choices.reason: This applies the factor exactly as defined in the problem.

correction.template: The effective contact time is {effective_time} min and CT is {ct} mg·min/L.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Reach CT=45 without changing the tank or flow
gates.constraint: Keep V=0.50 MG, Q=24 MGD, and baffling factor=0.70.

options.label: Keep residual at 1.5 mg/L
options.reason: That produces CT=31.5 under the stated effective-time definition.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply the same method to another basin

options.label: 57.6 mg·min/L
options.reason: Nominal time=60 min, effective time=48 min, and CT=1.2×48=57.6.

options.label: 72 mg·min/L
options.reason: That uses the nominal 60 min without the baffling correction.

options.label: 48 mg·min/L
options.reason: That is the effective time in minutes, not CT.

gates.explanation: Apply the stated effective-time factor before multiplying disinfectant residual by contact time.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the disinfection contact calculation
gates.confirmation: I confirm that a stated baffling factor must be applied to theoretical detention time before calculating CT when the problem defines CT using effective contact time.

seo.seo_title: Disinfection Contact Time and CT With Baffling | FE Environmental E-073
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Environmental Case E-073: a 0.50 MG tank at 24 MGD has 30 min nominal detention but only 21 min effective contact at a 0.70 baffling factor.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FE Environmental disinfection contact time CT
seo.excerpt: Nominal detention time is not always the effective contact time used in disinfection calculations. Apply the hydraulic correction stated in the problem.
seo.direct_answer: The theoretical detention time is (0.50/24)×1440=30 min. With a baffling factor of 0.70, effective contact time is 21 min. At a residual of 1.5 mg/L, CT=1.5×21=31.5 mg·min/L.

faqs.q: How is theoretical detention time calculated from tank volume and flow?
faqs.a: Use t=V/Q and convert the resulting time units as needed.

faqs.q: How is CT calculated when an effective contact time is specified?
faqs.a: Use CT=C×t_effective, after applying the stated hydraulic correction to nominal detention time.
